reasoning: Both sets fully plan all three environments with a shared core, hand-written learners, held-out test seeds, significance testing and replays, so the margin is narrow. A stays faithful to the stated success bar: every environment, including the co-evolved predator-prey agents, must beat both a random and a scripted baseline. It also covers reward shaping (EXP-05), which the brief lists as a target concept. Its RL experiment design is careful: numerically checked tank constants (warning time, no-tunnelling argument), sanity gates before any learner counts (TEXP-01 tank-too-easy check, HEXP-01 balance check), a well-reasoned opponent-pool schedule, and real co-evolution diagnostics (gen-8-vs-gen-1 progress test, cycling share, forgetting). Its Given/When/Then criteria are concrete and precise throughout. A loses points for process residue: superseded AD-02 and AD-10 stubs, inline '(changed ...)' markers across the spec, and history narration such as 'Nothing is built yet'. It also never updated CORE-01 for predator-prey, uses a Snake-era framing in CORE-03, has a predator truncation-versus-termination slip, and gives weak build-order guidance. B is the more pedagogical plan. Its DQN, policy-gradient and co-evolution ladders isolate one fix per step, the interactive viewer shows Q-values and policy spread, it compares full and limited vision, and it runs matched-hyperparameter reference checks and an honest power analysis. That makes its structure and next steps clearer for a learner. But B lowers the user's success bar to '≥75% of scripted' and says outright in the brief that beating the scripted player is not required. It puts alternative rewards (reward shaping) out of scope, never judges the simultaneously co-evolved agents against baselines, has no predator-prey balance gate, and sets a TANK-09 70%-in-view threshold that is very likely infeasible. Its brief also keeps tombstoned goals, and the idea files cite a goal that no longer exists. On balance A's fidelity and testability edge out B's pedagogy and structure.
